substance P (SP) induces the expression of macro phage inflammatory protein (CCL20), which plays an important role in periodontitis or orthodontic tooth move ment.
SP induces expression of HO‐ 1 and CCL 20 through the activation of the p38 MAPK and ERK1/2 pathways in human PDL cells.

SP induces the release from PDL cells of chemokine (C‐C motif) ligand 20, a chemotactic cytokine that attracts T lymphocytes and immature dendritic cells, and that SP‐induced CCL20 production is mediated by p38 MAP kinase, ERK1/2 and NF‐κB pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism by which SP regulates the expression of CCL 20 in IPDL.
the role of the SP/HO‐1/CCL20 axis in periodontal disease.
a novel mechanism by which SP induces CCL20 in human PDL cells, and the role of the HO‐1 pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP‐induced CCL20 is mediated by the p38 and ERK1/2 MAPK pathways, which are activated by the SP‐induced phosphorylation of IKB, degradation of IKB, and the subsequent activation of NF‐κB.
SP is involved in the expression of HO‐ and NF‐κB‐mediated CCL20 in human PDL cells.

SP induces CCL20 in PDL cells through activation of p38, ERK1/2, and NF‐κB signaling pathways.

The main takeaway from our work is that
SP is a potent inducer of MIP‐3α/Ccl20 in IPDL cell, and that this induction occurs via the p38 and ERK1/2 signaling pathway.

SP‐induced HO‐1 production may play a critical role in regulating the expression of MIP‐3α/C‐C ligand (CCL)20 in PDL cells, which is a potential target for therapeutic interventions in periodontal diseases.
